title: Cooperation beyond the dyad: The emergence and stability of animal societies
title_zh: 超越二元合作：动物社会的出现与稳定
abstract: Cooperation is a fundamental driver of social evolution, yet we still lack an integrated framework explaining how interactions among individuals scale up to the formation and long-term stability of animal societies. Although major advances have been made, research has often focused on a narrow set of model taxa and on individual mechanisms in isolation, hindering a comparative understanding across species and theoretical approaches. In this review, we synthesise theoretical and empirical work to link the processes that initiate group living with those that sustain cooperation once groups are established. We first examine how cooperation promotes the emergence of social groups through byproduct benefits, mutualistic interactions, and population viscosity, highlighting their differing dependence on relatedness and their potential to operate simultaneously in nature. We then review mechanisms that maintain cooperation within established groups- including reciprocity, assortment and population structuring, division of labour, policing and punishment- and consider how their importance varies across socioecological contexts and levels of relatedness. Finally, we outline how emerging tools, such as long-term behavioural datasets, social networks, comparative analysis, simulations and experimental manipulations, can expand research beyond a small set of well-studied systems and support comparative tests to improve our understanding of the processes shaping cooperation and social complexity across diverse taxa.
abstract_zh: 合作是社会进化的根本驱动力，但我们仍缺乏一个整合框架来解释个体间互动如何放大为动物社会的形成和长期稳定。尽管已取得重大进展，研究往往聚焦于有限的模型物种和孤立的个体机制，阻碍了跨物种和理论方法的比较理解。在本综述中，我们综合理论与实证研究，连接启动群体生活的过程与群体建立后维持合作的机制。首先，我们考察合作如何通过副产品效益、互惠互动和种群粘性促进社会群体的出现，强调它们对亲缘关系的不同依赖以及在自然界中可能同时发挥作用的潜力。随后，我们回顾维持已建立群体内合作的机制——包括互惠、分组与种群结构、劳动分工、监管与惩罚——并探讨其重要性如何随社会生态背景和亲缘水平而变化。最后，我们概述新兴工具，如长期行为数据集、社会网络、比较分析、模拟和实验操纵，如何扩展研究范围，超越少数研究系统，并支持比较检验，以提升我们对塑造合作与社会复杂性的过程的理解。
